text.p: Standard and Poor's Corp said on Thursday it has assigned its BBB-plus corporate credit rating to Woodside Petroleum Ltd.

S&P said the rating reflected Woodside's cost-competitive operaitons, strong and predicatable cash flow form long-term domestic gas and liquefied natural gas (LNG) contracts, and long reserve life of its fields.
These strengths were offset by the company's limited diversity and vulnerability to oil prices and currency movements, S&P said.
"The strengthening of Woodside's business position in the past two years should underpin a strong and consistent operating performance in the medium-term," the credit rating agency said.

"This strengthening primarily reflects expansion of the company's LNG and domgas contracts, lifting these facilities to near full capacity, completion of the North West Shelf Joint Ventures' asset base, and increasing diversification into oil, with start-up of the Laminaria-Corallina oil project in early 1999," S&P said.
Woodside's revenues were expected to reach about A$1.5 billion in fiscal 1999, with commencement of the Laminaria-Corallina oil project in the Timor Sea.

"While Woodside's exploration acreage largely is limited to two offshore regions, northern Western Australia and the Timor Sea, these are among Australia's most highly prospective oil and gas regions," S&P said.

At 1996 production rates, the company's reserve life stood at 32 years for gas and 25 years for liquids, giving Woodside considerable flexibility to withstand volatile oil prices and to adjust capital spending as market conditions dictate.
S&P said Woodside's rating outlook was stable.

"Woodside's strong operational characteristics, and greater diversification into oil with the expected commencement of the Laminaria-Corallina project, coupled with the company's commitment that its expansion plans and reserve development programme remain consistent with a moderate financial stance, should ensure stable credit quality in the medium term," S&P said.
Woodside is about 40 percent owned by the Royal Dutch Shell Group.
